title: Monolith architecture
idea: A monolith is one application deployed as a single unit. Every feature runs in the same process and usually shares one database.

analogy.text: One restaurant kitchen cooks every dish. Staff pass things hand to hand, which is fast, but the kitchen opens, closes and expands as a whole.
analogy.breaks: A monolith can still be organised into clean modules inside.

points: Every feature is a module in one codebase, built and deployed together.
Modules call each other as plain function calls, with no network between them.
One shared database lets a single transaction cover several features.
The cost: you deploy and scale as one unit; a crash can stop everything.

messages.label: POST /orders
messages.note: One request enters the one running application.

messages.label: orders calls payments
messages.note: A plain function call inside the same process: no network to cross.

messages.label: INSERT order
messages.note: All modules share one database, so one transaction can cover the whole change.

messages.label: committed
messages.note: A transaction commits together or rolls back together.

messages.label: 201 Created
messages.note: One process answers. Shipping a fix to any module means deploying the whole app.

code.title: Two modules, one process
code.caption: `orders` calls `payments` like any other function. Nothing can time out between them.

pitfalls: Do not split into microservices, the next page, just because monoliths sound old-fashioned.
Do not let modules read each other's database tables; call their functions instead.

quiz.q: What does the snippet print, line by line?
quiz.why: `charge(20)` returns true, so the order is placed. `charge(0)` returns false, so the payment is declined.

takeaway: A monolith is the simplest design; split it only for a real reason.
